- Repo root: `/content/bakeoff/quizrepo`

## Objective
- Make Variant A's MTD quiz render full-screen with normal page scrolling (no modal panel / inner-scroll container), fixing the bottom "Before continuing" banner clipped at 1280x720 and 1024x540 (Q2 answer "Yes, but I haven't shared it with them yet").

## Important Details
- Repo root: `/content/bakeoff/quizrepo`; target: `ongoing_project/MTD/variant-a/index.html`; server `python3 -m http.server 8150`; Playwright available in `node_modules`.
- **Generated, never hand-edit:** `variant-a/index.html` and `variant-b/index.html` are outputs of `ongoing_project/MTD/build-variants.js` from single source `mtd-income-tax/index.html` (2872 lines). Edit source or build script, then `node ongoing_project/MTD/build-variants.js` (`--check` = exit 1 if stale).
- **Quiz app is a frozen compiled bundle** — no source: `mtd-income-tax/quiz/assets/index-DhlXhpMI.js` (236394 B) + `index-NZKFqOaV.css` (40068 B); same bundle at `ongoing_project/MTD/page/quiz/`. Stable external selectors only: `Questions-styles__*` and suffixed tokens `fGtfKe/kyStRA/hnTQsX/lScyZ/hSoqJU/eAvKFB/hePGzN/jroPAt/kwDpZY/gomnIV/hntNzi`.
- State rule (repo guideline, `skills/shared/states.md` via `skills/ROUTE.md`): "Write rest, hover, focus, and active before editing any of them."
- AGENTS.md: one look per button class (`button--secondary`, `button--primary`, `button-tertiary`); spacing on `--sp-*` (4px); never claim done without gate evidence + rendered screenshots.
- Current architecture: hero CTA (`[data-mtd-quiz-trigger]` in `.score-stripe`, via `a.button-checkout` fallback) → `quiz-modal.js` dialog `#mtd-quiz-modal` (fixed, inset 0, focus trap, Esc) → iframe `#mtd-quiz-modal-frame`; `quiz-page.css` `.mtd-quiz-frame` min-height 640px; `variant-quiz.js` (259 lines) auto-advances entry card (`/start your mtd check/i`, 40×250ms), injects `variant-quiz-figma.css` when page has `.mtd-quiz-modal--figma-a`, fits iframe height, rewrites progress fill %, swaps Q1 icons, hides helper line/support CTA; `quiz-frame.js` auto-height (min 640) listening to `mtd-quiz:event` + MutationObserver/ResizeObserver, file:// falls back to CSS min-height.

1: /* Keep the embedded quiz flush with its own content so the iframe never grows
2:    an inner scrollbar. Same-origin static hosting: read the document height and
3:    follow the quiz's own screen-change event. Under file:// the read is blocked
4:    by the browser's opaque origin; the CSS min-height then keeps the frame
5:    usable. */
6: (function () {
7:   var frame = document.getElementById("mtd-quiz-frame");
8:   if (!frame) return;
9:   var timer = 0;
10: 
11:   function fit() {
12:     try {
13:       var doc = frame.contentDocument;
14:       if (!doc || !doc.documentElement) return;
15:       var height = Math.max(
16:         doc.documentElement.scrollHeight,
17:         doc.body ? doc.body.scrollHeight : 0,
18:         640
19:       );
20:       if (height > 0) {
21:         var next = Math.ceil(height);
22:         if (Math.abs(frame.getBoundingClientRect().height - next) > 1) {
23:           frame.style.height = next + "px";
24:         }
25:       }
26:     } catch (error) {
27:       /* file:// opaque origin: leave the CSS min-height in place */
28:     }
29:   }
30: 
31:   function soon() {
32:     window.clearTimeout(timer);
33:     timer = window.setTimeout(fit, 50);
34:   }
35: 
36:   function watch() {
37:     fit();
38:     window.setTimeout(fit, 300);
39:     window.setTimeout(fit, 1200);
40:     try {
41:       var win = frame.contentWindow;
42:       var doc = frame.contentDocument;
43:       if (!win || !doc || win.__mtdHeightWatch) return;
44:       win.__mtdHeightWatch = true;
45:       win.addEventListener("mtd-quiz:event", soon);
46:       var observer = new MutationObserver(soon);
47:       observer.observe(doc.documentElement, {
48:         subtree: true,
49:         childList: true,
50:         attributes: true,
51:         characterData: true,
52:       });
53:       if (window.ResizeObserver) {
54:         new ResizeObserver(soon).observe(doc.body || doc.documentElement);
55:       }
56:     } catch (error) {
57:       /* file:// opaque origin */
58:     }
59:   }
60: 
61:   frame.addEventListener("load", watch);
62:   window.setInterval(fit, 250);
63:   window.addEventListener("resize", soon);
64: })();

- Repo root `/content/bakeoff/quizrepo`; target `ongoing_project/MTD/variant-a/index.html`; serve `python3 -m http.server 8150`; Playwright in `node_modules`.

> **EXECUTED 27 Oct 2026.** Both prototypes are built and verified; see

> the promo strip is *not* missing from the HTML (it is the sticky nav banner), and

## 1. What Figma actually has (verified, not quoted)

| Frame | Node | Size | What the render shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Variant A — before | `3767:2716` | 1920 × 14408 | Full page, no banner, no inline quiz. Hero carries the primary **Get free MTD software** plus a **secondary** button `3792:4262` ("Take the MTD check"). Includes the promo strip "Get a further three months' free MTD software". |

| Variant B — full page | `3795:3228` | 1920 × 15107 | Gradient intro panel `3810:4255` (1920 × 595 at y = 120): eyebrow "Check. Connect. Check your details, connect your account and catch up with your first update to HMRC.", CTA **Start the MTD check**. |
| B — inline quiz | `3801:4228` | 1920 × 595 | The same "Get your tailored MTD guidance" panel, placed at y = 2948 (after the pricing cards). |
| B — "state 2" | `3810:4267` | 1920 × 595 | Visually **identical** to the inline quiz: same title, Step 1 of 7, same Q1 cards. Placed at y = 9084. |

Evidence: `render-A-before.png`, `render-A-modal.png`, `render-A-hero-ctas.png`,
`render-B.png`, `render-B-intro.png`, `render-B-inline-quiz.png`, `render-B-state2.png`.

## 2. What the HTML has today

Three files, and the registered one is a **hybrid of both variants**:

| File | Variant | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mtd-income-tax/index.html` | B + A combined | 240 KB, registered on the hub. Banner above the hero, inline quiz **immediately after the hero** (§1b), plus the Variant A modal. |
| `page/index.html` | B | Banner + inline quiz, no modal. Not registered. |
| `page/index-modal.html` | A | Modal only, no banner/quiz. Not registered. |

Measured deltas against Figma:

1. **Hero:** the page has exactly one CTA ("Get free MTD software", `a.button-checkout`,
   href `#getstarted`) and `quiz-modal.js` hijacks that primary link to open the modal.
   Figma A wants the primary untouched and a **secondary "Take the MTD check"** as the
   trigger. This is the most user-visible mismatch.
2. **Banner copy:** HTML reads "I've received a letter or message from HMRC about MTD" /
   "Find out where you are in the journey and what to do next". Figma B reads "Got a letter
   from HMRC? Don't panic" with the eyebrow, body and "Start the MTD check". Different
   section, not a reskin.
3. **Quiz placement:** HTML puts the quiz directly after the hero; Figma B puts it after
   the pricing cards (y = 2948 of 15107).
4. **Promo strip:** "Get a further three months' free MTD software" is present in the Figma
   variants and **absent** from the HTML page (`further`/`three months` find nothing).
5. **The double quiz in B** (y = 2948 and y = 9084) has no HTML counterpart at all.

## 3. Approach

Do **not** hand-copy the 240 KB page twice more — that is the duplication defect the quiz
audit just found (two byte-identical 2 MB trees, one edit applied in one place only).

- **One source, two generated outputs.** A builder derives both prototypes from
  `mtd-income-tax/index.html` with explicit, asserted patches per variant, and refuses to
  write if an anchor it patches is missing. The outputs carry a `generated — do not edit`
  header, like the other generated files in this repo.
- **Placement that keeps relative paths working.** Each variant is a folder with its own
  `index.html` (`ongoing_project/MTD/variant-a/`, `variant-b/`) so the hub discovery finds
  it (`**/index.html` only), with `<base href="../mtd-income-tax/">` so `assets/`, `quiz/`,
  `quiz-page.css` and the gate scripts resolve unchanged. If `<base>` trips the gate or the
  modal's iframe in the browser check, fall back to rewriting those four prefixes in the
  build.
- **Shared behaviour stays shared.** `quiz-page.css`, `quiz-frame.js`, `quiz-modal.js`,
  `a11y.js` and the quiz build are referenced, never copied.
- **No variant switching at runtime.** Two URLs, two screenshots, two verify specs — that
  is what "shown as prototype" needs, and it keeps each page diffable against its frame.

## 4. Steps

| # | Step | Gate / proof |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Fidelity diff first.** Section-order diff of `mtd-income-tax/index.html` against `3767:2716` and `3795:3228`: headings, CTAs, section order, then decide per delta whether Figma or HTML is authoritative. Output `FIDELITY.md`. | Every delta has a ruling; no silent "match Figma" on sections that came from the live export. |
| 2 | `build-variants.js`: emits `variant-a/index.html` and `variant-b/index.html` with per-variant patches (hero secondary CTA + modal trigger, banner vs gradient intro, quiz placement, promo strip, B's second quiz block). `--check` mode fails when an output is stale. | Builder asserts every anchor it patches exists exactly once; `--check` green. |
| 3 | Wire the interactions: A — secondary CTA opens the modal, primary keeps `#getstarted`; B — "Start the MTD check" scrolls to the inline quiz (or opens the modal — see §6 Q3). | Taps asserted at 1440 / 1000 / 390 in each variant's `verify.json`. |
| 4 | Register both in `hub.config.json` `MTD.pageOrder` and regenerate the hub with `HUB_PORT` pointed at this checkout. | `node tooling/hub-build.js` writes 2 new MTD cards; hub links resolve. |
| 5 | Screenshots per variant at 1440 / 1000 / 390 plus the modal open state; store beside the Figma renders so A↔A and B↔B can be put side by side. | PNGs present; no `#888888` placeholders. |
| 6 | Gate chain on the new pages: `check-page-gate.js`, `sync-check.js`, `check-markup.js`, `check-route.js`, `verify-section.js` per variant. | All exit 0; open FAILs reported, not waved through. |

Sequencing note: step 1 decides whether step 2 is a patch of the HTML page or a rebuild of
sections from components. Do not start step 2 before that ruling.

## 5. Why this is not just "add a button"

- The modal currently steals the primary conversion link. Fixing that changes the
  conversion path on the registered page, so it needs its own tap assertions at three
  widths (already in `verify.json`, which will have to be split per variant).
- B's gradient intro is a new section that has no component. It either gets harvested into
  `components/` (per the repo's library-first rule) or is documented as page-local. That is
  a C-7-style decision, not a styling choice.
- Three pages now share one quiz. If the dedupe from the quiz audit lands first, the
  prototype work does not have to touch two quiz copies.

## 6. Rulings needed before any build

1. **Authoritative side per delta** — where Figma and the HTML disagree (banner copy, promo
   strip, quiz placement), which wins for the prototype?
2. **The double quiz in Variant B** — is `3810:4267` (y = 9084) a genuine second state
   (e.g. after an answer) or a duplicate to delete? The render is identical to the inline
   one, so shipping both would show the quiz twice.
3. **B's CTA target** — "Start the MTD check" should scroll to the inline quiz or open the
   modal? Figma B has an inline panel, so scroll is the literal reading.
4. **A's promo strip** — the Figma variant carries "Get a further three months' free MTD
   software" but the HTML page does not. Include it in the prototype?
5. **URLs/names** — `variant-a` / `variant-b` under `ongoing_project/MTD/`, or keep them as
   `page/index-modal.html` / `page/index.html` and register those instead?

## 7. Risks

- `<base href>` is the one novel mechanism here; the fallback (rewrite four prefixes in the
  build) is mechanical and already scoped.
- Variant B is 15,107 px tall; a full-page render at readable scale is many megabytes, so

# Variant A / B HTML prototypes — built and verified

Roadmap 4.17, 2026-10-27. Figma: file `NcVP4hGOouCZHJkIYJR4tb`, page `3370:69660`
"Quizz". Figma was read only; nothing was written to the canvas.

## What now exists

| URL | Source | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `/ongoing_project/MTD/variant-a/` | generated | Full page, no quiz banner, no inline quiz. Hero carries the primary **Get free MTD software** plus a secondary **Take the MTD check** that opens the quiz modal (dialog 1520 wide). |
| `/ongoing_project/MTD/variant-b/` | generated | Full page. Gradient "Got a letter from HMRC? Don't panic" intro at the top (above the hero), inline quiz in the HMRC-letter slot after pricing, hero keeps its single primary CTA and is not wired to the modal. |

Both are generated from `mtd-income-tax/index.html` by
[build-variants.js](../../build-variants.js), which is the file to edit. Hand edits to
the two `index.html` files will be overwritten, and `--check` fails when they are stale.

Shared files gained additive-only changes, scoped so the registered page is untouched:

- `quiz-page.css` — `.mtd-hero-ctas`, `.mtd-hero-quiz-cta`, `.mtd-quiz-intro*`,
  `.mtd-quiz-modal--figma-a` (1520 dialog width).
- `quiz-modal.js` — the trigger is now `[data-mtd-quiz-trigger]` if present, else the old
  `a.button-checkout`. The registered page carries no attribute, so its behaviour is
  unchanged.
- `variant-quiz.js` — new, loaded only by the two variants.

## How the build maps to Figma

| Figma | Node | Implemented as |
|---|---|---|
| A — before click, 1920 × 14408 | `3767:2716` | Registered page minus banner and inline quiz; hero button group now carries `Take the MTD check` (`3792:4262`) as a secondary. |
| A — modal open, 1920 × 1080 | `3776:6405` | Existing 4.11 modal, widened to 1520 to match the 1520 × 597 quiz body in the frame. |
| B — intro, 1920 × 595 at y = 120 | `3810:4255` | `<section class="mtd-quiz-intro">`: eyebrow pill, H2 with green accent, body, CTA **Start the MTD check**; empty left column as the frame's spacer. Copy is verbatim. |
| B — inline quiz, 1920 × 595 at y = 2948 | `3801:4228` | The quiz section moved from after-the-hero into the HMRC-letter slot; the HMRC-letter block it displaced is the intro at the top. |

Because both frames draw the quiz at **Step 1 of 7**, `variant-quiz.js` clicks through the
compiled quiz's entry card once on load (the bundle has no deep-link support). The page CTA
has already asked the visitor to take the check, so this is the state the design shows.

## Verification

`node tooling/verify-section.js` — **ALL PASS** for both pages at 1440 / 1000 / 390
(section present, images load, no stretched images, no horizontal overflow, no failed
requests, no page errors, CTA tap assertion).

`node ongoing_project/MTD/.work/roadmap-4-17/shoot.js` — **16/16 PASS**:

- A: no quiz banner · no inline quiz section · hero CTAs exactly
  `[Get free MTD software, Take the MTD check]` · modal present · modal opens from the
  secondary CTA · dialog 1392 wide at 1440 (1520 clamped by the 24px modal padding) ·
  modal renders Step 1 of 7.
- B: no quiz banner · intro present · intro above the hero · quiz after pricing · hero has
  exactly one CTA · old HMRC-letter block gone · modal not bound · intro title and CTA
  match Figma copy · inline quiz renders Step 1 of 7.
- Both: no horizontal overflow at 390.

Screenshots (this folder): `variant-a-hero-1440.png`, `variant-a-modal-1440.png`,
`variant-b-intro-1440.png`, `variant-b-quiz-1440.png`, `variant-a-390.png`,
`variant-b-390.png`.

Gates run: `sync-check`, `check-markup`, `check-route` — all exit 0; `check-page-gate`
and `check-spacing` fail only on pre-existing, untouched files (see §Corrections).

## Deliberate deviations from the frame

1. **Variant A's dialog keeps the approved 4.11 shell** (title bar with Close, plus a
   "Close the quiz" footer). Figma draws only the quiz body with a cancel icon at
   top-right. Dropping our close affordances to match the picture would cost keyboard and
   pointer users their visible exit, so the shell stays; width now matches at 1520.
   Ruling needed if the frame's chrome is the intent.
2. **The gradient is CSS, not art.** Figma uses a glow artwork with gradient rectangles;
   the card recreates the look with layered radial gradients (purple lower-left, teal
   right) so no new asset enters the repo.
3. **Card width follows the page container** (`1440` max), so at a 1440 viewport the card
   fills the container rather than sitting at Figma's 1440-within-1920 with 240px margins.
   Same proportions at 1920.
4. **B's "state 2" quiz artboard (`3810:4267`) is not implemented.** It is a top-level
   frame *outside* the B page (the page's 16 children contain exactly one quiz section),
   and it renders identically to `3801:4228` — same Step 1 of 7, same Q1. Shipping it as a
   second block would show the quiz twice.

## Corrections to earlier notes

- **The promo strip is not missing.** An earlier note (roadmap 4.14 / PLAN.md) claimed the
  variants carried a "Get a further three months' free MTD software" strip absent from the
  HTML. That was a misread of a 0.12-scale render: the strip is the sticky nav banner
  ("HMRC signed you up for MTD? Submit your first update with free MTD software"), which
  the HTML has. Figma's pricing block carries the 90%-off promo cards, and the HTML pricing
  block is the same block the registered page already ships.
- **Pre-existing gate failures, not caused here:** `check-page-gate.js` fails on
  `components/cn09-skinny-banner/preview.html` (gate scripts missing) and
  `check-spacing.js` fails on `components/agent-guidelines/canvas.css:80`
  (`margin-bottom: -1px`). Both files are committed on `draft`, untouched by this change,
  and fail the same way without it.

## Still open

1. A ruling on the Variant A dialog chrome (deviation 1).
2. Whether `3810:4267` is a real second state that still needs drawing.
3. Hub regeneration: `hub.config.json` now lists both pages under MTD, but `index.html`
   was not rebuilt because another worker was mid-edit on the Compatabilite pages and
   `hub-build` re-shoots every project. Run `HUB_PORT=<port> node tooling/hub-build.js`
   when the tree is quiet.
4. Independent review (repo doctrine: the builder's own report is not sign-off).
